name: Faze Three Ltd
tagline: Record-revenue home-textiles exporter whose profit fell 24% YoY on an input-cost shock -- weak returns and a rich multiple with no clear inflection
business_overview: Faze Three is a vertically integrated manufacturer and exporter of home textiles and technical textiles (yarn to finished product), focused almost entirely on export markets.
fundamentals_table: Revenue Rs 235 Cr, up 8.9% YoY (highest-ever June quarter); PAT Rs 9.64 Cr, down 24.5% YoY
fundamentals_narrative: Q1 FY27 revenue was the company's highest-ever for a June quarter, but that top-line record didn't translate to earnings: EBITDA fell 5% YoY and PAT dropped 24.5% YoY, as cotton, polyester, chemicals, fuel, packaging and logistics costs rose 25-35% from pre-war levels amid the West Asia crisis, only partially offset by better USD/INR realisation. Trailing ROCE (8.25%) and ROE (6.52%) were already weak before this margin hit, and the stock trades at a rich ~47x P/E for that return profile. Cash flow from operations was a genuine bright spot (Rs 48.2 Cr, aided by working-capital release), funding capex and a modest debt reduction.

bear_case: PAT fell 24.5% YoY even as revenue hit a record -- a genuine, current margin problem, not a one-off base effect
Trailing ROCE (8.25%) and ROE (6.52%) were already weak before this quarter's cost shock

verdict_headline: Record revenue, but profit is moving the wrong way and the multiple doesn't fit the return profile

The cost shock driving the margin miss (West Asia-linked input inflation) is an ongoing, unresolved headwind rather than a one-off already absorbed
